title: Meeting transcripts: who can create them, where they live and who can read them
summary: The controls, defaults, licensing statements and storage rules are supported by Microsoft's documentation. One open question should be removed: although the cited pages do not explain retention precedence, other Microsoft documentation does.

claims.claim: Meeting and group-call transcription is managed at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Transcription.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. Toggle Transcription On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows transcription for the policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "Your Policy Name" -AllowTranscription $true

claims.claim: Transcription for events up to 1,000 attendees is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Transcription for events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select the policy that you want to edit or create a new one. Turn the Transcription for events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: The transcription guide documents Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TranscriptionForWebinar $true to allow event transcription.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TranscriptionForWebinar $true

claims.claim: Copilot is configured at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn selects the saved-transcript default that organizers can change.
claims.quote: To set the organizer's default Copilot option to During and after the meeting and allow them to change it, use the following script: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot EnabledWithTranscriptDefaultOn

claims.claim: Automatic expiration is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Recordings and transcriptions automatically expire setting in the Teams admin center under Meetings > Meeting policies > Recording & transcription.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days> sets the default expiration time.
claims.quote: To set the expiration time using PowerShell, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days>

claims.claim: Graph transcript access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Transcript API access > Microsoft Graph access.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings. Under Transcript API access, turn the Microsoft Graph access toggle On to allow apps and agents to access meeting transcripts.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -EnableGraphTranscriptAccess $true enables Graph transcript access for the organization.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -EnableGraphTranscriptAccess $true -EnableAttributedTranscripts $true -Identity Global

claims.claim: Graph speaker attribution is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Transcript API access > Microsoft Graph access > Configure > Include speaker attribution.
claims.quote: Select Configure, and then do the following: To include speaker attribution in transcripts accessed through Graph API, turn the Include speaker attribution toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -EnableAttributedTranscripts $true enables speaker attribution in Graph transcripts.
claims.quote: To configure transcript API access by using PowerShell, use the Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration cmdlet with the following parameters: -EnableAttributedTranscripts: When set to true, transcripts accessed through Graph APIs include speaker attribution.

claims.claim: Real-time Work IQ transcript access is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting settings > Transcript API access > WorkIQ access.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting settings. Under Transcript API access, turn the WorkIQ access toggle On.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess $true enables real-time transcript access through Work IQ.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -EnableWorkIQTranscriptAccess $true -Identity Global

claims.claim: A transcript is the written record of what was said in a Teams meeting or event.
claims.quote: Transcription creates a real-time written record of what was said during a meeting or event.

claims.claim: Participants can view the saved transcript with timestamps and speaker attribution.
claims.quote: Participants can view the transcript after the meeting along with timestamps and speaker attribution.

claims.claim: Transcripts are stored with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint.
claims.quote: Transcripts are stored together with meeting recordings in OneDrive and SharePoint storage.

claims.claim: Large-audience event transcription uses the TranscriptionForTownhall parameter of Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy.
claims.quote: To manage transcription for events optimized for large audiences by using PowerShell, use the -TranscriptionForTownhall parameter in Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy.

claims.claim: Transcription for events up to 1,000 attendees is on by default.
claims.quote: Turn the Transcription for events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off. This setting is On by default.

claims.quote: Turn the Transcription for events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off. This setting is On by default.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy reference marks the policy as preview.

claims.claim: The events-policy reference types TranscriptionForWebinar as String, unlike the guide's Boolean example.
claims.quote:
-TranscriptionForWebinar
Determines whether transcriptions are allowed in events up to 1,000 attendees.
Possible values are:
Enabled: Allow transcriptions in events up to 1,000 attendees.
Disabled: Prohibit transcriptions in events up to 1,000 attendees.
Type: | String

claims.claim: The events-policy reference gives Enabled as the transcription parameter's default.
claims.quote: Default value: | Enabled

claims.where: Open questions: auto-apply retention label policy and expiry
claims.claim: The pages cited by this concept do not explain how an auto-apply retention label interacts with expiration.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams recording expiration auto apply retention label policy expiration retention priority transcripts. Read the cited storage, expiration and sensitive-meetings pages; the explanation is instead in manage-teams-recording-compliance and Purview retention guidance.
claims.fix: Remove the open question beginning 'How does an auto-apply retention label policy interact with the expiry setting'. Its qualification 'on the pages read' is accurate, but the question is answered elsewhere: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-teams-recording-compliance explains retention versus expiration, and https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/retention-policies-sharepoint states that permanent deletion is suspended when the item must be retained by a retention policy or retention label. No replacement paragraph is needed.
